name: Tuzla
title: Tuzla Shipyard Gauging: In-Dock UTM for Steel Renewal
description: Thickness gauging in the Tuzla shipyards: in-dock UTM of bottom, side shell, tanks and holds on bulk carriers, tankers and ro-ro ships under steel renewal.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement in the Tuzla Shipyard Zone, Istanbul
intro: Tuzla, on the Anatolian shore of the Sea of Marmara at Istanbul's eastern edge, is the heart of Turkish shipbuilding and ship repair. Its floating docks and repair quays take bulk carriers, chemical tankers, ro-ro ships, tugs and ferries for renewal surveys, steel renewal and conversion, while newbuilding berths turn out tugs and small tankers. Here gauging is part of the yard programme rather than a cargo call. The technicians are flown in from India for each docking and work to the yard's sequence.

highlights.h: Readings ahead of the steel order
highlights.p: Tuzla yards plan plate orders, cutting and welding gangs from the thickness report, so the first readings set the shape of the docking. We measure the areas most likely to need renewal first and hand them over to the superintendent and the yard's steel department area by area.

Once renewed inserts are welded in, adjacent plating that was near the allowable diminution is measured again, so the final TM report shows the ship as it leaves the dock rather than as it arrived. That is the record the class surveyor closes the survey items against.

Scrubber, ballast water treatment and conversion work in the Tuzla yards opens up shell, tanks and pipework that are normally hard to reach. Gauging existing structure before new foundations or shell penetrations go in shows whether the steel can carry them.

port.h: Tuzla: Istanbul's shipyard district on the Sea of Marmara
p: Tuzla sits at the eastern end of Istanbul's Anatolian side, where the city meets Kocaeli province, on the north shore of the Sea of Marmara. Shipbuilding came here after 1969, when yards that had worked for generations on the Golden Horn and the Bosphorus were moved out to Aydınlı Bay, and the shipyard zone has since filled the shores of the bay and the coast beside it with yards, slipways, floating docks and fitting-out quays. The water is sheltered and the tidal range negligible, so docking and undocking are governed by the yard's programme and the weather rather than by the tide. Winter gales, above all the south-westerly lodos, are the main operational interruption, and ships waiting for a dock lie at the anchorages a short launch ride from the quays.

The zone mixes newbuilding and repair. Some yards specialise in tugs, ferries, fishing vessels, offshore support ships and small chemical tankers, a market in which Turkish builders have long been strong in Europe; others are mainly repair yards with floating docks of different sizes and long repair quays; many do both. Repair customers include Turkish owners from around the Marmara, Greek and other European managers, and Black Sea and Mediterranean operators who want a yard close to their trading routes. The ships that come in for docking are mostly Handysize and Supramax bulk carriers, chemical and product tankers, general cargo ships, ro-ro and ro-pax ships, LPG carriers and offshore vessels, with tugs, ferries and coastal tankers filling the smaller docks between them.

What sets Tuzla apart from a cargo port is that ships come here to be opened up. Tanks are cleaned and ventilated, holds are blasted, staging is rigged for the class surveyor's close-up survey, and steel renewal is decided, ordered and fitted in the space of one docking. That compresses the inspection work into a tight sequence: pre-docking estimates to fix plate quantities, in-dock measurement of bottom and side shell while the hull is dry, tank and hold gauging as spaces are released, and re-gauging around renewed areas before undocking. The yard's own trades, the superintendent, the class surveyor and the gauging team all work from the same thickness report, which is why its timing and layout matter so much in Tuzla.

facilities.h: Docks and quays where gauging is done in Tuzla
p: Floating docks are the workhorses of Tuzla ship repair, ranging from small units used by tugs, ferries and coasters to large docks that lift Supramax bulk carriers and product tankers. Bottom plating, bilge strakes, sea chests, the stern frame and rudder plating are measured while the ship is dry, and the repair quays take over for decks, internal structure, hatch covers and piping once the ship is afloat again. Gemak, which runs floating docks and a graving dock, and the Tuzla repair branch of Tersan, better known for newbuilding at Yalova, are among the yards that take ocean-going ships for docking and steel renewal.

Each yard runs its own gate, permit-to-work and gas-free procedures, and the gauging team works within them, usually alongside blasting, staging and hot work in neighbouring spaces. Ships waiting for a dock lie at the anchorages off the yard zone, where pre-docking readings can be taken by launch. When a ship moves between yards, or docks in Tuzla and then completes work afloat at the Altınova yards across the water, the same measurement plan and point numbering follow it so the final report reads as one survey rather than two.
list: Floating docks across the yard zone — bottom, bilge, side shell, sea chest and rudder plating gauged while the ship is dry.
Graving dock at Gemak — larger ships and conversion projects, with in-dock gauging alongside the class surveyor's close-up survey.
Repair quays — gauging of holds, tanks, decks, hatch covers and piping before docking and after undocking.
Conversion and retrofit berths — gauging of existing structure before scrubber, ballast water treatment or conversion steelwork.
Anchorages off the yard zone — pre-docking readings on ships waiting for their dock date, reached by launch.
Altınova yards in Yalova, across the water — work continued afloat or a second docking within the same trip.

context.h: Regulation and repair-yard practice at Tuzla
p: Turkey is a member of both the Black Sea MoU and the Mediterranean MoU, and many ships arrive in Tuzla with port state control deficiencies from Black Sea, Marmara or Mediterranean ports still to be cleared, typically wasted air pipe heads, ventilators or deck plating. Ship movements and the anchorages around the yard zone are overseen by the local harbour master under the Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure, and yard work on tanks that have carried oil or chemicals needs gas-free certification before hot work, which also governs when a gauging team can go in. Class surveyors attend the yards daily during dockings, so readings that arrive late hold up the surveyor as well as the steelwork.

In practice, the gauging report drives the yard's technical and commercial decisions at once. Tuzla yards estimate steel renewal by weight and plan plate orders, cutting and welding gangs from the areas marked for renewal, and the undocking date follows from that plan, so a ship that arrives with a measured pre-docking estimate and is gauged in the order the yard needs keeps its schedule. Ships trading on to EU ports also carry obligations such as an Inventory of Hazardous Materials and EU ETS reporting, and yard work that adds new equipment, coatings or insulation should be reflected in the ship's IHM before it sails.

jobs.h: Gauging work we see in the Tuzla yards
jobs.p: Almost every Tuzla job is tied to a docking date. A superintendent sends the survey status, the last TM report and the yard's work list, we agree with the yard which spaces will be ready on which days, and the team arrives for pre-docking readings at anchor or for the first days in dock. After that the work follows the yard: shell while dry, tanks and holds as they are certified, and re-gauging around renewals before undocking. Smaller jobs come from tugs, ferries and coastal tankers that dock here at regular intervals, and from conversion projects where existing structure has to be assessed first.
list: Bottom and side shell gauging on a Supramax bulk carrier in a Tuzla floating dock during its fourth renewal survey, with hold frames measured as holds are blasted.
Sea chest, overboard and scrubber wash-water penetration gauging on a product tanker while dry, before shell doublers are cut out and replaced.
Re-gauging of plating around renewed inserts on a general cargo ship's main deck before undocking, completing the TM report for class.
Condition gauging of existing structure on a ro-ro ship before a conversion, with readings marked against the conversion drawings.
Hull and tank gauging on a harbour tug and a coastal tanker at their periodic docking.
Magnetic particle testing of stern frame and rudder horn welds after cracking was reported during a docking inspection.

logistics: Istanbul Sabiha Gökçen Airport is the nearest airport to the yard zone, with Istanbul Airport on the European side as an alternative, and the yards are reached by road along the Anatolian shore. Yard entry needs a gate pass and safety induction organised by the yard and the owner's superintendent, and anchorage boarding uses a launch the ship's agent books. Each technician travelling from India needs a Turkish visa, so we start the application once the docking date is agreed and plan for the slot moving, which in repair yards it often does.

faqs.q: When should the gauging team arrive for a Tuzla docking?
faqs.a: Ideally before the ship enters dock. Readings at anchor off the yard zone or at the last cargo port let the yard order plate and plan labour before the ship is lifted. If that is not possible, we start on the first day in dock with the bottom, side shell and the spaces most likely to need renewal, so the steel list can be fixed while the rest of the ship is measured.

faqs.q: Can you measure sea chests, rudders and the stern area while the ship is dry?
faqs.a: Yes, and a docking is the only practical time to do it. Sea chest plating, the stern frame, rudder plating and the shell around overboard penetrations are measured once the hull has been cleaned. Where cracking is suspected at rudder or stern frame welds, magnetic particle testing can be done in the same visit, subject to access and the yard's hot-work programme.

faqs.q: Do you work with the yard's steel department during renewal?
faqs.a: Yes. We pass readings to the superintendent and, where agreed, to the yard's steel department as each area is finished, with locations marked on drawings and, if requested, on the structure itself. That lets cutting start on confirmed areas while measurement continues elsewhere, and afterwards we re-gauge the plating next to each renewal so the final report reflects the ship as it undocks.

faqs.q: Can one mobilisation cover several ships in Tuzla?
faqs.a: Often. The yard zone is compact, and owners and managers frequently have more than one ship docking in Tuzla or at Altınova within a few weeks. If you share the docking dates, we plan a single trip with a visa period that covers them and sequence the work so each yard receives its readings when it needs them.
